column1: v0.3 — High-Level PRD for PM/BA Review

Black Box is a modular, AI-powered POS platform for retail businesses of any vertical (apparel, grocery, convenience, general merchandise, F&B retail), operating single or multi-branch, with or without an online storefront. Beyond transaction handling, it turns sales data into operational decisions through AI-driven reordering, inventory redistribution, and pricing, while keeping offline and online inventory in sync.

Retailers are stuck between lightweight POS tools that only ring up sales, and enterprise ERPs that are unaffordable and over-engineered for SMBs. In between sits real pain — stockouts, overstock, inventory drift between branches and marketplaces, cash-handling errors, weak audit trails, and reactive pricing. Black Box targets that middle.

• Reliable offline-first POS at the counter, across verticals and store formats.
• AI recommendations owners can act on in one click (reorder, shuffle, price).
• Real-time inventory truth across branches and online channels.
• Configurable depth — a boutique needs a fraction of what a hypermart needs; both feel native.
• Pluggable regional fiscal/tax compliance.

• Full accounting/ERP replacement.
• Payroll, biometric attendance, or HR system.
• Warehouse management at fulfillment-center scale.
• Document management (licenses, contracts) beyond basic uploads.
• Custom AI models per tenant.

Retailers running 1–20+ branches across apparel, grocery, convenience, F&B retail, and general merchandise. Primary buyers are owners; day-to-day users are branch managers and cashiers. Secondary: accountants, warehouse managers (where applicable).

Two-axis billing: modules enabled × number of branches. Unlimited cashiers/users per branch. Base tier = Core POS. Add-ons: each AI feature, Two-Tier Inventory, Expiry Module, Third-Party Concessions Module, each marketplace integration, Fiscal Adapter.

column3: AI needs 2–3+ months of clean data to be useful. First-tenant experience risks being underwhelming.
column4: Rule-based fallbacks for first 60–90 days; vertical templates seed sensible defaults.

column3: Grocery (perishables, weights) vs apparel (variants, sizes) have different data models. How much generalize vs specialize?
column4: Design core schema with type extensions per vertical; ship vertical templates (Grocery, Apparel, Convenience, F&B Retail).

column3: Marketplace APIs (esp. Daraz, Foodpanda) have rate limits and quirks. Sync SLAs need definition.
column4: Adapter pattern; retry + backoff + reconciliation tools; document per-marketplace SLAs.

column3: Owners may not act on AI recommendations if they don't understand or trust them.
column4: Show reasoning, confidence, expected impact; feedback loop into training.

column3: Highly modular product risks painful setup. Onboarding could take days.
column4: Ship vertical templates with sensible defaults; guided onboarding wizard.

column3: Each country/regime is real engineering (FBR, ZATCA, GST e-invoice, EU printers).
